sections.h2: Who bills and who values in Chatham County
sections.html:
Two offices stand behind every Chatham bill. Values and exemption approvals come from the Board of Assessors. Billing, collection and distribution of the money to each taxing body come from the Tax Commissioner, whose office takes no role in valuation or millage.

The Tax Commissioner's 2026 brochure lists the bodies billed on one statement: the county, the Special Service District, the school board, transit, and the cities of Garden City, Pooler, Port Wentworth, Thunderbolt, Tybee Island and Vernonburg. Which ones apply depends on your address, and your bill's line items show it.

  • Tax Commissioner: 912-652-7100, tax.chathamcountyga.gov, offices at 222 W. Oglethorpe Ave., 295 Police Memorial Dr. and 1145 Eisenhower Dr., open weekdays from 8:30am until 5:00pm.
  • Board of Assessors: 912-652-7271, boa.chathamcountyga.gov, Suite 113, Pete Liakakis Government Building, 222 West Oglethorpe Avenue.
  • Mail: Chatham County Tax Commissioner, P. O. Box 9827, Savannah, GA 31412.
  • Three satellite tax offices, on Wilmington Island Road, US 80 and Georgia Highway 21, take appointments only.

Georgia's northernmost coastal county is Chatham, home to Savannah, the seat. Of its 632 square miles, 206 are water. Besides Savannah there are seven municipalities: Bloomingdale, Garden City, Pooler, Port Wentworth, Tybee Island, Thunderbolt and Vernonburg.

Population climbed from 295,291 in 2020 to an estimated 311,855 by mid-2025. The 2020 to 2024 survey puts the median owned home at $302,700 and typical rent at $1,471 a month, with 56.8% of households owning. Builders pulled 4,426 permits during 2025.

Land and buildings are billed in halves, due June 1 and November 15. Business and other personal property gets a single bill, also due November 15.

The first real property bill goes out by April 1 and the second by September 15. Payment can be mailed to P. O. Box 9827, Savannah, GA 31412, made online, or made in person. Credit card and eCheck payments online carry convenience fees, although the brochure says eChecks are free. A returned check or eCheck is charged 5% of the amount, with a $30 minimum, under O.C.G.A. 16-9-20.

Anything unpaid on the due date is delinquent and draws interest and penalties. A delinquent parcel may also carry a tax lien, which a title company will want cleared first.

sections.h2: How to appeal your Chatham County assessment
sections.html:
Deliver a written challenge to the Board of Assessors within 45 days of the date on your Annual Notice of Assessment. It is that notice, and not a tax bill, that starts the clock. Georgia provides a uniform appeal form, and the allowed grounds are taxability, value, uniformity or a denied exemption.

On that first appeal you name your method. The brochure lists three:

  • Board of Equalization, then Superior Court if you still disagree.
  • Arbitration, which requires a certified appraisal submitted within 45 days. The Board of Assessors can accept or reject it, and you may still petition Superior Court.
  • Hearing Officer, available only for non-homestead real property worth $500,000 or more, or certain wireless property above $200,000 in total value.

Bring recent sales, photographs of similar homes that sold, and lease or income figures. The Board measures square footage around the outside perimeter, so a smaller interior living area alone does not prove an error.

Returns can be filed from the start of the year through April 1, using forms on the assessors' website. Your first return rolls over yearly at the last final value. Disagree with that figure? File a new return stating your own value, which keeps your appeal rights intact if the Board revises it again.

Farmland in active use may be assessed at 30% of market value rather than 40%, and conservation use land is valued at its present use. Both need a covenant to keep the use for at least 10 years, so find out from the Board what a sale does to it before listing.

The regular exemption takes $12,000 of assessed value off the county levy and $2,000 off the school and state levies. For any homestead exemption you must own the house, live there and claim it as your legal residence on January 1, so rentals do not qualify.

  • Stephens-Day and the state floating homestead exemption: the county awards whichever saves more, then adds any other exemptions you qualify for.
  • Special Chatham senior exemption: age 65 by January 1, combined net income of $10,000 or less, $30,000 off county and school assessed value, plus relief from most state assessments.
  • Senior school exemption: age 62, combined net income of $25,000 or less.
  • Exemption for a 100% service-connected disability: bring a VA letter, and note the amount can change each year.
  • Year's Support: when a spouse or minor child petitions Probate Court within two years after a death, the court can award tax relief for the year named in the petition.

Applicants need a Georgia driver's license or ID and a vehicle registration in their name, with the mailing and homestead addresses matching. An application received inside the 45-day notice window counts for that year, and a later one is held for the next. Buying another home or changing the deed means filing again.

sections.h2: Who pays when a Chatham County house sells?
sections.html:
You are billed as the seller, since Georgia taxes whoever owned the property when the year began. Selling in March or August does not shift the bill to the buyer, and no refund is given for part of a year.

Splitting the year is a private arrangement made at closing. A sale between the June and November deadlines leaves the second installment open, so ask the closing attorney whether it is paid at the table or credited to the buyer. Include any delinquent balance in the payoff so no lien stays with the title.

The exemption belongs to you, so the new owner files separately. If you inherited the house, reread the Year's Support option above. Before settling on a closing day, request a payoff from the Tax Commissioner at 912-652-7100.

Look up your parcel on the assessors' site to see the value and exemptions on file, and ask the Tax Commissioner whether either installment is open. For a house in a city such as Pooler or Tybee Island, the same office bills the city share, so the payoff should cover every line. Cash buyers ask for the same payoff letter, and having it in hand keeps closing on schedule.

faqs.q: Do Chatham County owners pay once or twice a year?
faqs.a: Real property is paid in two halves, June 1 and November 15. Personal property is a single payment on November 15.

faqs.q: Which Chatham County office answers valuation questions?
faqs.a: Call the Board of Assessors, 912-652-7271. The Tax Commissioner, 912-652-7100, collects payments and cannot alter a value or millage rate.

faqs.q: Is there any appeal once the 45 days run out?
faqs.a: Usually not. The deadline runs from the notice date, and if a notice never reached you, ask the Board of Assessors what options remain.

faqs.q: Does a buyer inherit my homestead exemption?
faqs.a: No. The exemption stays with the person who filed, and a purchaser must apply fresh at the Board of Assessors with a Georgia license and a matching vehicle registration.

faqs.q: Will I owe tax if I sell in the fall?
faqs.a: Yes, for that year, since you held title in January. A still-open November installment shows up on the closing statement as a payoff or a credit.
